candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
H.R.1049 adds a condition for local educational agencies to receive Elementary and Secondary Education Act funds: each school they serve must give parents specified access to information about foreign-supported materials, personnel and financial arrangements. The proposed Health connection is this explicit condition on the same local-agency funding stream that includes Student Support and Academic Enrichment grants. Under 20USC7115–7118 those grants may fund school-based mental-health services, identification, counseling referrals and qualified mental-health partnership programs. This is a funding-eligibility condition across a broad education statute, not a new mental-health appropriation, clinical treatment mandate or demonstrated reduction in services.

A parent must be able to review and make free copies of covered curricular or professional-development material, consistently with copyright law, at least every four weeks and within 30 days of a written request. Within 30 days of a written request the school must disclose how many personnel are compensated in whole or part with covered foreign funds, and information about donations, written agreements and financial transactions with a foreign country or foreign entity of concern. The information includes the country or entity name and, where funds were received, their amount and terms. Each school must post an annual summary notice or widely disseminate it if it has no website. The Education Secretary must notify States annually; States must notify local agencies as their own condition of receiving ESEA funds. These are disclosure duties, not a prohibition on every foreign donation or a release of individual student medical records.

The incorporated foreign-entity definition includes designated terrorist organizations, Treasury-listed blocked persons, entities connected to the governments of the four covered nations, and the specified Attorney General or Commerce determinations. The four covered nations in 10USC4872(f)(2) are North Korea, China, Russia and Iran. Its defense-procurement prohibitions are not imported. The Attorney General category concerns alleged involvement in activities for which a conviction was obtained under the listed laws; the candidate does not adjudicate any entity or treat an allegation as an independently proven fact. The bill’s foreign-country definition excludes the ESEA outlying areas.

The existing grant framework remains. States allocate funds to local agencies with approved applications, using the specified prior TitleI share, with a $10,000 minimum subject to ratable reduction and permission for agency consortia. Local applications, consultation, needs assessment and annual reporting remain. The ordinary minimum 20-percent allocation to safe-and-healthy-student activities is not a mental-health earmark: multiple activities qualify, and grants below $30,000 have a special rule allowing only one of the three activity-category assurances. No particular school or provider is shown to lose funds, and no resulting service interruption is inferred.

Existing care safeguards also remain. TitleIV generally requires informed written parental consent for school-connected mental-health assessment or services for children under 18, with immediate-safety and specified unobtainable-consent exceptions. It prohibits medical services, drug treatment and rehabilitation except integrated student supports, specialized instructional support services and treatment referrals; it does not authorize unrestricted clinical spending. Specialized support includes the defined professional services and limited related services, whose medical component is diagnostic/evaluation and excludes surgically implanted devices and replacement. The separate limits on program content and mandatory medication remain. The December4,2025 House passage vote concerns the whole disclosure-and-funding-condition bill. A Yea supports that condition; a Nay opposes it without establishing opposition to parental information or support for undisclosed foreign influence. Neither choice alone establishes a position on mental-health services generally.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
candidate_dispositions.reason:
S.356 extends Secure Rural Schools payments through fiscal 2026 and requires the fiscal 2024 and 2025 payments within 45 days after enactment, reduced by the specified revenue-sharing payments already received or distributed before enactment. It carries forward the counties’ fiscal 2023 payment and allocation elections for 2024 and 2025 and extends the California distribution provision through 2026. The existing payment formulas and allocation rules remain: generally 80–85 percent follows the applicable school/road or county-fund use, with the remaining balance allocated to permitted projects or returned. Counties receiving at least $350,000 may allocate at most 7 percent of the total payment to Title III; counties receiving less than $100,000 may use all funds under the ordinary payment purposes. This is a broad county-funding package, not a medical-services appropriation alone.

The proposed Health connection is the extension of Title III county-project authority. It moves the project-initiation deadline from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2028 and the deadline after which unobligated funds must be returned from September 30, 2026 to September 30, 2029. Incorporated 16 U.S.C. 7142 permits reimbursement of county-paid search-and-rescue and other emergency services performed on Federal land after approval, and directly related training/equipment. Uses require a 45-day public comment process and proposal to the relevant resource advisory committee; expenditure certification remains required. A pre-vote first-party Skamania EMS and Rescue report documents a $25,000 Title III award toward a patient-access and transport vehicle, with other costs met by its general fund. This supplies a concrete emergency-medical-response use of the authority, not a claim that every emergency service is clinical care, every county selects that use, or every use of that vehicle is federally reimbursable.

Title III also permits Firewise work, community wildfire plans and specified school broadband/digital-learning access; those uses are retained. Title II land-management project initiation and obligation deadlines likewise move to 2028 and 2029. The bill extends the resource advisory committee composition waiver and appointment pilot authorities to October 1, 2026, removes the pilot-program report-to-Congress requirement and makes limited wording/date corrections. It does not remove all committee oversight, public participation or project requirements.

The House considered the Senate-engrossed text under a motion to suspend the rules and pass on December 9, 2025, and agreed to it. The floor Record supplies the exact text and broader debate. Speakers’ predictions about school closures, services, employment, addiction and the reasons for timber-revenue changes are not adopted as proven outcomes or motives. Public Law 119-21 section 50301 separately directs receipts from specified long-term timber contracts to the Treasury general fund; S.356 does not repeal that provision, and the candidate does not treat all timber receipts as available county funds. The Health finding concerns the bounded emergency-response funding authority within one choice on the entire reauthorization.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
candidate_dispositions.reason: H.R.1676 changes the approval process for State wildlife conservation and restoration programs under16USC669c(e)(3): a180-day approval deadline, conditional implementation authorization and fund set-aside on plan submission, a review process developed with States, prioritization and a status/reason report to the named congressional committees by June1 of the following year if the deadline is missed. Conditional implementation is not automatic final approval; the existing compliance finding, Federal cost-share limit and program conditions remain. The incorporated program covers wildlife conservation, wildlife-associated recreation and conservation education;669a defines wildlife as fauna, and669g(a) preserves the education restriction concerning opposition to regulated taking. The separate hunter-safety/target-range provision in669g(b) is not amended. candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The exact December11 passage choice concerns the full H.R.3628 EH, including its GAO report. It adds a PURPA standard for State-regulated utilities employing integrated resource planning: measures for reliable electric energy over ten years through continued operation of, or procurement from, generation facilities meeting continuous thirty-day operation and on-site or contracted fuel-supply criteria, emergency/severe-weather operation and frequency/voltage support. Incorporated16USC2621(a)-(c) requires consideration after public notice/hearing and a written evidence-based determination, but permits a determination against implementation and permits declining an appropriate standard with written reasons. This is not automatic nationwide adoption of the new generation standard. The new deadlines apply to each State regulatory authority for the State-regulated utilities within its ratemaking authority: commence consideration or set a hearing within one year, determine within two. Prior implemented or considered comparable State standards qualify for the specified exception; the three-year limit attaches to the alternative State-legislature vote, not to every prior proceeding. Conforming changes address noncompliance and prior/pending proceedings. The GAO report within one year evaluates prior integrated resource planning and reliability, stability and affordability; incorporated2602 definitions concern electricity customers, resource alternatives and State ratemaking jurisdiction. No operative provision changes clinical care, health coverage, a household-assistance benefit or a Health-program funding condition. Possible consequences of electric reliability for hospitals or public health do not establish exact-action Health membership. This proposed exclusion does not assert that electricity is irrelevant to health or predict the bill’s consequences.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
The exact December11 passage choice is the full66,005-character H.R.3383 EH INVEST package, not merely the original closed-end-fund title or the three rejected amendments. The entire EH was read. It changes capital-formation advocacy, eligible fundraising communications and safeguards, crowdfunding financial-disclosure thresholds, private-fund adviser and venture-fund thresholds, SEC small-entity review and internal offices, investor accreditation and an examination pathway, retirement-plan investment exemptions, senior-investor oversight, electronic document delivery, closed-end-fund access to private funds and securities-registration/disclosure rules. It retains section307 multi-class-share disclosure, which roll325 unsuccessfully sought to strike; rejected foreign-client AML and No Junk Fee amendments326/327 are not imported into this passage.

Section202 changes securities-law treatment of qualifying403(b) custodial accounts, collective trusts and separate accounts, with specified ERISA, employer-fiduciary or governmental-plan conditions and investment-review protections. Bound15USC80a-3(c)(11),77c(a)(2),78c(a)(12) and78l(g)(2)(H) show those existing securities exemptions;26USC403(b)(1)/(7) identifies the underlying retirement arrangements. The existing403(b)(2) health/long-term-care distribution tax exception is expressly retained as context, not described as newly created, repealed or enlarged by this bill. Permitting retirement investment vehicles does not itself change that exception, Medicaid, Social Security or health coverage. Possible nonprofit health-provider employers do not convert this into a condition on clinical-program funds.

Section204 creates an SEC Senior Investor Taskforce using existing funds for investors over65, with a ten-year sunset, identifying exploitation/cognitive-decline challenges and coordinating as appropriate with the Elder Justice Coordinating Council and financial/law-enforcement authorities. Its reports recommend securities-regulatory and legislative changes; those recommendations do not implement themselves. The first-report clause references section3 of the named National Senior Investor Initiative Act of2025; this review preserves that wording and does not silently replace it with section204(b) or claim that the dependency is satisfied. The separate GAO study due within two years explicitly examines financial-exploitation costs including public-benefit/public-health programs, contributing factors such as illness and isolation, adult-protective-service reporting, agency limits and gaps, and barriers to coordination. These are material adjacent social-service references, not omitted because of the finance title. Bound42USC1397k confirms the existing Council’s HHS/Justice elder-abuse coordination and recommendation role. The bill neither rewrites that Council’s governing powers nor provides new adult-protective-service delivery, care funding, health-insurance eligibility or clinical research; its new SEC and GAO duties concern investor protection and financial exploitation. This proposed exclusion follows the declared exact delivery/financing boundary, not a claim that exploitation has no health consequences.

The package also retains opt-out paper documents, failure-remediation and disclosure-timing protections in electronic delivery, and preserves specified fiduciary, valuation, liquidity and redemption obligations in the closed-end-fund provisions. The complete package and nearby standalone amendment choices remain separate. No predicted cost, fraud, care or investment outcome is asserted.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
The full54,257-character H.R.3898 EH passed December11 is independently reviewed, including its26 sections and the complete proposed PartA amendments in Report119-399. This is substantive environmental/water legislation, not a procedural vote and not a Health exclusion inferred from its title. The exact package changes combined-sewer standards review and cost/technology considerations; requires rulemaking for new or revised water-quality criteria; changes water-quality certification scope, deadlines, enforcement and specified energy-certification judicial review; creates general-permit procedures and longer permit terms; broadens the described permit-compliance shield; and changes aerial fire-suppression, agricultural-stormwater and pesticide permit requirements. The pesticide exemption preserves its listed FIFRA-violation, stormwater, manufacturing/treatment-works and vessel-discharge exceptions.

It also limits the period for EPA disposal-site prohibitions to the completed-application/permit-issuance window, revises dredge/fill nationwide permits and environmental-review requirements, changes State-program applications and judicial review, ratifies the named Michigan/New Jersey/Florida programs subject to the stated congressional-withdrawal restriction, requires mitigation/permitting/backlog work, narrows navigable-water coverage and changes farm spill-control thresholds. Further provisions encourage FAST-Act coordination, express a cooperative Chesapeake approach, identify water-recharge lands and permitting processes, establish the voluntary nitrogen/phosphorus pilot, and allow the U.S. IBWC to accept qualifying funds for wastewater, conservation and flood-control works subject to appropriations, foreign-source restrictions and the annual$5million non-Federal credit/reimbursement cap. These are not health-insurance or care-service appropriations. The final text includes water recharge but not the separately proposed brackish-groundwater/desalination section; making an amendment in order is not evidence it became law or entered the EH.

Material public-health references are retained. Existing33USC1313(c) water standards protect public health/welfare;1314(a)(1)/(9) criteria include pollutant effects and pathogen indicators for coastal recreation. Section3 changes the method for adopting those environmental criteria, not a clinical-care or clinical-research program. Existing1342(k) expressly excepts standards for toxic pollutants injurious to human health; the EH adds scope language without striking that existing exception. New section15 limits judicial remedies but expressly allows specified permit/discharge relief for imminent and substantial danger to human health or the environment when no other equitable remedy exists. The fire-suppression heading concerns a discharge-permit exemption, not firefighter medical benefits. Section21 changes farm oil-spill certification/exemption quantities; the existing note confirms the separate single-tank and discharge-history rules and the animal-feed context. These source-grounded environmental-health connections do not establish the declared Health mechanism of care, insurance, Medicaid, Social Security or social-service delivery/financing. This proposed exclusion makes no prediction about illness, pollution, costs or safety outcomes and does not deny that environmental regulation can affect health.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
The entire H.R.2550 EH is the December11 passage choice: nullify the executive order titled Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs issued March27,2025, prohibit Federal funds to carry it out, and give collective bargaining agreements in effect March26 between an executive-branch agency and an exclusive employee representative full force through their stated terms. The bound EO14251 as issued is read completely. Its exclusions expressly include VA and named HHS components (FDA, CDC, ASPR, NIAID, refugee resettlement and others), and specified information-management subdivisions including SSA, alongside many other agencies. It also includes Foreign Service exclusions, Defense/VA suspension authority, a Transportation delegation, and implementation/grievance provisions. The immediate-local police/security/firefighter exception has its Bureau-of-Prisons limitation; named agency coverage must not be silently generalized to every employee or every HHS subdivision. The bill identifies the March27 order, not every later labor-related executive order; this review neither resolves litigation nor promises universal reinstatement.

The operative mechanism is Federal workforce bargaining and agreement duration, including health/social-service agency employees, not a change to the services or statutory benefits administered by those agencies. Bound5USC7103 defines bargaining over conditions of employment, excepts matters specifically provided by Federal statute, and supplies the named national-security exclusion authority. Bound38USC7421/7422 retain the separate Title38 rules for the listed VA clinical professions: bargaining does not cover professional conduct/competence (defined to include direct patient care and clinical competence), peer review or Title38 compensation determinations, with the stated Secretary determination and judicial-review channel. The bill does not amend these provisions or specify a new clinical staffing, treatment, Medicaid, Social Security, insurance or household-assistance entitlement. Preserving an existing agreement is not evidence of a particular unexamined agreement term, service outcome or medical benefit. This proposed exclusion follows the declared delivery/financing boundary while retaining the actual health-workforce connection; it does not infer that labor rights have no consequences for care. Keep roll321 discharge,331 rule adoption and332 substantive passage distinct.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The complete15,531-character H.R.3668 EH is reviewed as the December12 passage choice, separately from its recommittal. It makes FERC the sole lead agency for the specified Natural Gas Act section3 authorizations/section7 certificates, coordinates participating agencies and sets participation, review, information and reporting deadlines. Nonparticipating agencies face the stated supplemental-review exception and restrictions on submitted comments. Its water provision removes the section401 certification requirement for the covered Federal authorization, replacing that gate with State/interstate participation and proposed conditions that FERC may include only on the stated necessity finding. It is not merely a promise of faster coordination or automatic approval of every pipeline. Federal authorization deadlines are normally within90days after NEPA review unless Federal law supplies another schedule; a missed deadline triggers notice and an implementation plan. Remote-data conditional approvals require subsequent onsite verification; contractor assistance, public tracking and TSA security consultation are retained. Bound15USC717n,717b and717f identify the exact energy-authorization channel,33USC1341 the existing water-certification gate, and42USC4332 the environmental-review framework. These are energy/environmental authorization changes, including material water-quality conditions, not changes to clinical care, insurance, Medicaid, Social Security or social-service delivery/financing. No medical, price, safety or environmental outcome is inferred.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
candidate_dispositions.reason: The complete Senate-passed S.284 text is the December15 suspension-and-pass choice, not merely a nonbinding commendation. It extends the Congressional Award Board termination from October1,2023 to October1,2028 with retroactive effect as of the former date and removes the prescribed medal-material formula while retaining Treasury medal production. Bound2USC802 identifies the youth achievement program, including public service, personal development and physical/expedition fitness, achievement verification, presentation and discretionary scholarships. Those existing fitness, youth and scholarship references are preserved; they do not make the reauthorization a clinical, insurance or social-service delivery/financing measure under the declared Health boundary. The bill changes program duration and medal specifications, not medical treatment or a health benefit. Suspension-plus-passage is substantive legislation, while the proposed disposition is exact-action Health ineligibility.

candidate_dispositions.reason: The full H.R.3187 EH is the December15 suspension-and-pass-as-amended choice. candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
H.R. 4371 EH would change the Office of Refugee Resettlement’s care-placement system for unaccompanied children in federal immigration custody. It replaces 6 U.S.C. 279(b)(2) with a cross-reference to its replacement of 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(2), and adds sponsor-information requirements to the existing suitability process in 1232(c)(3). Health & Social Policy membership is proposed from the direct child-welfare placement, suitability and continuing-care mechanisms in those statutes, not merely the immigration topic, the HHS name or a predicted effect on crime. The existing definition covers children under 18 without lawful immigration status and without a parent or legal guardian in the United States available to provide care and physical custody. Placement includes detention and alternatives. This is one vote on the entire placement-and-screening package.

Before making a placement determination, HHS would consult DHS and the Attorney General, including appropriate juvenile-justice officials, about appearances, protection from exploitation, flight risk, danger and criminal history. For children 12 or older, it must contact the relevant foreign consulate or embassy for arrest, pending-charge and conviction records and examine the child for gang-related tattoos or markings. The least-restrictive, best-interest placement default remains subject to the new exceptions, and the existing prohibition on release on the child’s own recognizance is retained in the replacement provision. Children 12 or older who meet the flight-risk or danger conditions must be in a secure facility throughout immigration proceedings and, if ordered removed, until removal. The danger language includes gang-related markings, specified serious or aggravated-felony convictions, and arrests, charges, pending proceedings or convictions connected to gang affiliation/activity. A conviction is therefore not required for every secure-placement trigger. No numerical maximum detention period is supplied, and this candidate does not claim that the text resolves every external detention limit.

Sponsors must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents. Placement is barred if the sponsor or a household member has a listed conviction, including defined sex offenses, trafficking, domestic violence, child abuse/neglect, homicide or attempted homicide, child sexual-abuse-material offenses, crimes within the referenced immigration-custody authority, aggravated felonies, jurisdiction-defined felonies, crimes punishable by more than a year, or another offense designated by the Attorney General in the stated sole and unreviewable discretion. The incorporated definitions have limits: for example, the sex-offense definition excludes the specified insufficiently safeguarded foreign convictions and consensual conduct; severe trafficking includes the defined forced/coerced labor and sex-trafficking circumstances. The domestic-violence definition also discusses noncriminal conduct for victim services, but this bill’s placement bar requires a crime and conviction. The custody cross-reference is read with the January 2025 Laken Riley Act amendment to 8 U.S.C. 1226(c)(1), not only the older Code baseline; this does not erase the sponsor clause’s own conviction requirement or make a household member’s immigration status itself a conviction. Before an individual placement, HHS must give DHS identifying, immigration-status and contact information and background-check results for the sponsor and every adult household resident, including the stated sex-offender-site, public-record and fingerprint-based national checks.

Replacing all of 1232(c)(2) removes that paragraph’s express monthly secure-placement review and its age-18 transfer provision requiring consideration of the least restrictive setting and eligibility for detention alternatives. It also removes that paragraph’s express option for placing child-trafficking victims in the Unaccompanied Refugee Minor program when suitable family care is unavailable. Other provisions remain: 6 U.S.C. 279(b)(3) encourages use of the refugee-child foster-care system, whose incorporated 8 U.S.C. 1522(d) authority includes child-welfare, foster-care and health-care services; 1232(d)(4) separately retains its specified placement/service eligibility and conditional State reimbursement. The bill retains 1232(c)(3)’s physical and mental well-being suitability determination, specified mandatory home studies and follow-up services, and authorization for additional follow-up for mental-health or other needs. Separate legal-orientation, qualified access-to-counsel and child-advocate provisions, and ORR facility/placement oversight, are not repealed by this text. This is not a claim that all care protections disappear or that every child is guaranteed every service.

The package includes severability and conditional Paperwork Reduction Act/Administrative Procedure Act implementation language when specified officials determine compliance would impede immediate implementation; it is not a waiver of all law. It takes effect on enactment and specifies pending/future release and custody determinations and release redeterminations. Its applicability clause prints section642(g)(2), while the bound Homeland Security Act child definition is section462/6 U.S.C. 279(g)(2); the mismatch is preserved without silently correcting the printed proposal or ruling on its legal effect. The floor Record verifies adoption of the reported substitute under H.Res.951 and passage on December16. Stansbury’s formal motion was bare recommittal; her separately printed proposal to remove the markings examination was not part of the passed text. Supporters argued for screening and protection from dangerous placements; opponents disputed examination practices, sponsor restrictions and prolonged custody. Those claims about motives, current practices and future harm or safety are not adopted as proven facts. The vote does not reveal which provision determined a member’s choice.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The full H.R.3632 EH replaces Federal Power Act207. It permits qualifying transmission-organization complaints as well as State complaints, adds a hearing opportunity within90days and a five-year prospective inadequacy finding, permits orders to continue generation and specified interstate-transmission planning, and requires compensation rates/cost allocation. Orders last no more than five years with the stated request/hearing/extension process; the text does not supply a categorical one-extension ceiling. It retains the prohibitions on compelling generation-facility enlargement or energy sales that impair customer service. Actions or omissions necessary to comply with issued/extended orders, including voluntary compliance, receive the stated environmental-law nonviolation/liability/citizen-suit protection; this is a material qualification, not omitted as an incidental clause. Owners/operators must give five-year retirement notice for covered units of at least5MW connected to the bulk-power system, except specified unplanned events rendering a unit inoperable. The retirement definition includes indefinite idling/disconnection/unavailability. Bound16USC824f supplies the replaced authority and824o(a) the grid definition. These are electricity-service, compensation and environmental-law mechanisms, not care, insurance, Medicaid, Social Security or social-service delivery/financing. No health outcome from reliability or emissions is assumed.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution
candidate_dispositions.reason: The exact rejected H.Con.Res.61 is read in its introduced text and verified against the text printed on the December 17 floor. It directs removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with presidentially designated terrorist organizations in the Western Hemisphere, with the stated declaration-of-war/specific-congressional-authorization exception, pursuant to War Powers Resolution5(c). The two resolutions have distinct geographic/target language and are not interchangeable. Bound50USC1544(c) provides the invoked concurrent-resolution mechanism; this record does not resolve constitutional disputes over that mechanism or existing hostilities. The proposed direction concerns military hostilities/authorization, not a medical service, drug-treatment program, health insurance or household assistance. Floor references to fentanyl, trafficking, death or humanitarian consequences do not turn it into an exact-action Health choice. This is proposed Health ineligibility, not a classification of the failed substantive war-powers direction as mere House procedure or a nonbinding statement of sympathy.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason:
H.R. 3492 EH would replace 18 U.S.C. 116, which already penalizes female genital mutilation of people under 18, with a broader set of federal offenses covering defined gender-transition surgeries and medication provision as well. Under the specified jurisdictional circumstances, knowingly performing or attempting the defined surgeries, or knowingly providing the defined medications, carries a fine, up to 10 years of imprisonment, or both. The ten-year maximum is also present in the existing FGM law; this bill expands the covered conduct rather than newly creating that maximum. The person receiving a covered procedure or medication cannot be arrested or prosecuted under this section. This is one passage vote on the entire criminal-law package, not the separate H.R. 498 Medicaid-funding choice.

For the new procedure/medication coverage, the purpose is changing the body to correspond to a sex different from the sex classification at birth, as defined in the bill. The text enumerates genital/reproductive surgeries, mastectomy, specified throat/voice-related surgeries, feminizing or masculinizing plastic surgery, chest/gluteal implants and urethral reconstruction for that purpose. Medication provision includes administering, supplying, prescribing, dispensing, distributing or otherwise conveying drugs for that purpose, including GnRH analogues or other puberty blockers to stop/delay normal puberty, testosterone/androgens to those defined as female and estrogen to those defined as male at the specified supraphysiologic doses. It does not prohibit every use of those drugs or every listed operation regardless of purpose. The bill separately retains a definition of nonmedical female genital mutilation and offenses for facilitating, consenting to or transporting a minor for that conduct. Its statutory labels are not adopted here as clinical judgments about transgender people or medical practice.

The licensed-practitioner exception covers procedures necessary to the minor’s health, but expressly excludes mental, behavioral or emotional distress and disorders from health for that exception. A separate FGM exception concerns medical procedures connected with labor or birth and the listed licensed practitioners, midwives or trainees. Further exemptions specify individuals with both ovarian and testicular tissue; the specified sex-chromosome, hormone-production or hormone-action findings established by physician testing; infection, disease, injury or disorder caused or worsened by a prior covered intervention; physician-certified imminent impairment of a major bodily function from a physical condition; and diagnosed precocious puberty when the intervention normalizes puberty. These are the text’s defined conditions, not an unrestricted medical-necessity exception or a medical conclusion about any individual.

The jurisdictional circumstances include specified interstate/foreign travel, instrumentalities, payments, communications, items that traveled in commerce, federal maritime/territorial jurisdiction or territories, and conduct otherwise in or affecting interstate/foreign commerce. Roy’s proposed four-category replacement in Report119-411 was made in order but expressly not offered according to the floor Record; it is not imported into the passed bill. The printed FGM facilitation/transport subsection(c) refers to(d), while(d) says it is for(a)/(b) and repeatedly names those subsections. This candidate preserves that drafting mismatch without deciding its legal consequences or claiming that(c) is unenforceable. Nor does it infer a universal parent-liability or parent-immunity rule from the distinct FGM wording.

The Record separately shows Balint’s bare recommittal motion and her previously referred proposed effective-date instructions. The displayed proposal would condition effectiveness on a Comptroller General determination concerning medical records and prosecution; it was not the formal bare motion and is not in the EH. The House passed the bill December 17 after rejecting recommittal. Floor speakers disputed clinical evidence, family decision-making, federal power and prosecution effects. Their empirical and motive claims are not treated as established medical facts. Support or opposition here concerns this exact criminal-law proposal, with its definitions and exceptions; neither direction supplies a broad position on all gender-related care or all child protection.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The complete H.R.4776 EH changes NEPA environmental review, authorization stability and judicial review. It adds functional-equivalence routes using other statutes or State/Tribal review, restricts considered effects to the specified immediate/proximate causal scope, changes new-research duties and timing, and binds other agencies to specified lead-agency no-document determinations. It restricts changes to completed environmental documents and project authorizations, while retaining the printed existing-law/savings qualifications, court-order, violation/fraud, specified immediate substantial life/property/security harm, and holder-request exceptions. It includes written notice, evidence and appellate review requirements, an applicant-consent restriction on Federal remand petitions, and a negative-no-action presumption for qualifying Tribe-initiated trust-resource actions. Application-completeness and review scheduling, cooperating-agency participation, final-action deadlines and applicant-approved extensions are changed; final action within30days after an assessment/statement is not an automatic permit approval. It extends programmatic reliance from5to10years while preserving the substantial-new-information qualification, permits reuse/augmentation of prior reviews, broadens categorical/major-action exclusions including specified farm loans, and adds energy alongside retained health goals in CEQ’s advisory duties. Judicial review is limited by deference, remand without vacatur/injunction under the specified APA ground, participation/direct-harm and150-day filing conditions, tribal-trust exceptions, and court/appeal schedules; the supplemental-document deadline wording and separate deadline-enforcement provision are not silently rewritten. The July2025 project-sponsor opt-in fee provision is renumbered, not newly enacted by this bill. Section4 excludes specified agency actions reopened/remanded/corrected betweenJanuary20,2025 and enactment regardless of completion, as deemed under H.Res.953. A token-level RH/EH comparison finds this section4 as the operative addition; failed floor amendments1/5/6 are not imported. These are environmental-review, permitting and litigation mechanisms, with express human-health/life qualifications retained, not a direct care, insurance or social-service delivery/financing change under the declared Health boundary. No safety, pollution, litigation-cost or medical outcome is inferred.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The complete H.R.1366 EH permits as many reasonably necessary mill-site claims as needed within the approved mining plan on eligible public land, including mineral, nonmineral or unclassified land. Each single site remains limited to5acres; the new mill site conveys no mineral rights, is not patentable, may overlap the claimant/operator’s earlier lode/placer claim and does not change that claim’s validity. Existing withdrawals and specified regulatory powers/rights, and Public Law118-42 divisionE404’s patent-processing funding limitation and exceptions, are preserved. The fund receives maintenance fees collected on the new sites, not every existing mining fee; Interior may spend without further appropriations only for30USC1245 abandoned-hardrock-mine reclamation. That authority expressly uses public health/safety and environmental need among priorities, divides allocations50percent State/Tribal grants and50percent Federal lands, permits Agriculture transfers, limits eligible land/water and excludes fulfillment of court/settlement CERCLA obligations. It finances reclamation/hazardous-release response, not treatment, insurance or individual social-service assistance; those public-health priorities are not erased to justify exclusion. Incorporated operations/operator and mineral/nonmineral definitions are read in2025CFR pages; the September2025 amendatory instructions leave the latter two definitions unchanged. The bill’s future-enactment-date regulatory references are not represented as a known future version. No aggregate5acre ceiling, automatic project approval, cleanup outcome or new fixed$3billion appropriation is inferred. The proposed Health exclusion rests on the operative land-use and remediation mechanisms.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Passage
candidate_dispositions.reason: The exact H.R.5184 reported substitute, adopted under H.Res.977 and passed January9, replaces DOE’s mandatory manufactured-home energy-standard program with discretionary recommendations to HUD’s separate preemptive energy standards. These are building-performance mechanisms, not a direct medical-care, insurance or individual social-service benefit. The housing/affordability title and possible utility-cost, indoor-air or health consequences do not establish membership under the declared Health boundary. The July2,2025 compliance amendment already replaced the original2023date with60/180days after publication of final enforcement procedures for the two tiers; do not claim the older2023date was still the operative deadline at this vote. The bill removes the specified rule rather than merely extending that deadline. Incorporated engineering calculation manuals are identified by the rule but are not independently validated here; no quantitative energy, household-cost, ventilation-health or safety outcome is inferred. No new housing subsidy or care-delivery program is supplied by the complete bill.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
candidate_dispositions.reason: The January12 amended suspension text and EH concern control of foreign remote access to US-jurisdiction items under the Export Control Reform Act. The Secretary must determine a serious national-security or foreign-policy risk. The definition includes purposeful, knowing, reckless or negligent access but expressly does not lower criminal mens rea. The bill extends general control, licensing, enforcement, penalty, reporting and confidentiality machinery to remote access; Congress must be kept informed, without a new prior-approval requirement. Complete directly amended ECRA sections and the retained50USC1702(b) exceptions were reviewed. The latter include conditional humanitarian donations of food, clothing and medicine, as well as personal communications, information and travel. These retained general-control limits are material contrary evidence, but this exact action does not establish a medical-supply-specific licensing rule, clinical access, insurance, or Health/social-service delivery or financing. Possible medical uses of computing and references to biological-weapons risks do not supply that missing mechanism. Unlike the separately reviewedH.R.5334 medical-transaction carveouts, this proposal adds a general remote-access control category without a new medical-transaction provision. Propose exclusion under the existing direct-mechanism boundary, not a finding that export policy can never affect health. FousheeYea/MassieNay remain recorded evidence, not the reason for membership. The House passed the amended bill; no enactment is inferred.

candidate_dispositions.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments
candidate_dispositions.reason: The Senate text struck only section 1 of the House bill, inserted a new Division A concerning Russia sanctions and Iran-sanctions authorization, and added a Division B heading before retained House section 2. The retained provision extends the educator-expense deduction to qualifying early-childhood educators for expenses in tax years after 2025. The new sanctions cover specified Russian persons, banks, vessels, energy and related transactions, with import duties, waivers, congressional review and termination provisions. Section 114(a) exempts medicines, medical devices, humanitarian assistance and related transactions from Title I measures; it also addresses covered international agreements with Ukraine subject to a presidential sanctions-evasion determination. Section 114(e) separately excepts low-enriched uranium or medical isotopes imported under the specified statutory waiver. These are conditions on medical-supply transactions within a sanctions package, not a new domestic health benefit. Section 201 extends the Iran Sanctions Act expiration to 2031, while section 203 sunsets the other new authorities after five years.
